methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Rhoman Aerospace is a seed-stage company operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation universe consists of seven private peers in this space, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in the narrowly defined peer set. The sector remains highly fragmented across application verticals—cargo delivery, urban air mobility, and specialized logistics—limiting direct comparability.

The peer-median approach is not applicable to this valuation. While five same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the filtering criteria for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier companies. The dataset contains zero qualifying datapoints at seed stage within Drones & Autonomous, zero at adjacent stages, and zero at similar valuation tiers. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of business models, regulatory pathways, and market maturity across the peer set.

Given the absence of sufficient narrow peer data and the early stage of Rhoman Aerospace, traditional comparable-company triangulation cannot produce a defensible valuation range. Alternative approaches—including comparable transactions in early-stage autonomous systems, venture capital method based on exit assumptions and required returns, or asset-backed analysis—would be required to establish valuation support. The primary uncertainty remains the lack of homogeneous peer data at seed stage in this emerging sector.
